forecaster_note: Looking like a good morning of surf with size hitting the 2ft-overhead range for the standout magnets around the region, and something more easy size wrapping to other breaks. Similar size PM. Winds will be light and offshore early and it's well worth making the time for. Sea breezes into the afternoon will drop quality for most spots as surf gets textured around midday and then more bumpy PM, but the south-facing breaks will stay cleanish. – Surfline forecast team. Water temp is estimated (no live station feed this run).

wind.summary: Light WNW offshore to ~10am, then an E sea breeze textures it from midday.

shark.summary: SharkSmart check pending this refresh — tap to check live detections

days.label: Today
days.note: Best of the three days. Solid S swell at 100% consistency with light WNW offshore until roughly 10am. Long Reef and Curl Curl carry the real size — Dee Why is softer because the swell is sitting dead S at 185° and wraps in gutless. Energy peaks around 200 kJ, so it is punchy-but-not-heavy: quality over grunt. Get on it before the E sea breeze arrives midday.

dee-why.window: 5:52am–10:00am — glassy WNW offshore on a rising tide toward the 12:55pm high.
alerts: Swell is dead S 185° — wraps soft into Dee Why. Long Reef and Curl Curl get the real size today.

tip.label: Skip the Point
tip.text: At 185° the Point corner will be gutless. Walk down to the beachie banks — the rights there are your frontside, sit wide of the peak and let the 8s SE component swing them in.

long-reef.window: 6:00am–10:00am — pick of the coast. Cleanest and biggest before the breeze swings E.

tip.label: Frontside walls
tip.text: Biggest and cleanest of the four. Rights off the northern bank are frontside. The 9s period means longer lulls — be patient and take the set wave, not the first one through.

curl-curl.window: 6:00am–10:30am — south-facing, so it stays cleanish even once the breeze fills in.

tip.label: South corner
tip.text: The south end takes the S swell best. Lefts there are backside — set your rail early off the bottom, the 8s SE mix makes them square up fast.

manly.window: 6:00am–10:00am — smallest of the four, easy paddle-out.
alerts: Half the size of Long Reef — North Steyne is shadowed from this S angle.

tip.label: Softest option
tip.text: Only worth the drive if you want an easy one. North Steyne banks will be thigh-to-chest and crumbly once the E breeze arrives after midday.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Shorter S swell fades but a long-period S fills in behind it — more power per wave, longer lulls between sets. Energy drops to ~160 kJ and consistency falls to 74%, so expect waiting. Offshore all morning, light NE sea breeze later. Some banks will be quite straight; find a good one.

dee-why.window: 6:00am–11:00am — offshore all morning before the NE fills in.

long-reef.window: 6:00am–11:00am — best exposure to the new long-period S. Pick of the weekend mornings.

manly.window: Marginal — not worth it over Long Reef.
alerts: Too small and too shadowed from this angle.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Both days surfable, Sunday slightly bigger on paper (215 kJ peak) but consistency slips to 68% — more sitting than surfing. Offshore mornings both days with light cross-shore breezes after midday. Saturday morning at Long Reef is the standout window of the weekend. Neither day gets near your 450 kJ floor, so this is a rail-and-flow weekend rather than a step-up one.

alerts: S swell angle keeps wrapping soft into Dee Why all weekend.

long-reef.window: Saturday morning is the pick of the weekend — cleanest and most consistent.

curl-curl.window: Sunday builds through the morning — south end holds shape.

manly.window: Skip unless you want a small, easy session.
alerts: Shadowed all weekend by the S swell direction.
